nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a measurable map preserving a finite measure $\mu$, and let $E$ be a measurable set. Then for $\mu$-almost every $x \in E$ there are infinitely many $n$ with $T^n x \in E$: almost every point of $E$ returns to $E$ infinitely often.
nodes.title: Poincaré recurrence theorem

nodes.title: Furstenberg multiple recurrence theorem

nodes.summary: Sinai's entropy of a measure-preserving transformation measures the rate at which the dynamics produces information. A finite partition $\xi$ turns every orbit into a stationary sequence of symbols; the entropy of $T$ relative to $\xi$ is the Shannon entropy per symbol of that sequence, and the Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy $h_\mu(T)$ is its supremum over all finite partitions. nodes.title: Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy

nodes.summary: Every continuous map $T : X \to X$ of a nonempty compact metric space $X$ to itself has an invariant Borel probability measure: there is a probability measure $\mu$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $X$ whose pushforward under $T$ equals $\mu$.
nodes.title: Krylov–Bogolyubov theorem

nodes.summary: A measure-preserving transformation is mixing when every event, pulled back far enough along the dynamics, becomes asymptotically independent of every other event: $\mu(A \cap T^{-n} B) \to \mu(A)\,\mu(B)$. nodes.summary: A measure-preserving map $T$ acts on square-integrable functions by its Koopman operator $U_T f = f \circ T$, a linear isometry of $L^2(\mu)$. Von Neumann's mean ergodic theorem, the first ergodic theorem (1932), says that the ergodic averages $\frac1N \sum_{k<N} f \circ T^k$ converge in $L^2(\mu)$ to the orthogonal projection of $f$ onto the invariant functions.
